- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk premium or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply decay.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model misreads momentum; apply mean reversion bias toward 60–65% of recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling (e.g., +0.67 sentiment, -0.5% price), model overreacts; reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% for next 3 days.
- Model often ignores sentiment volatility in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days); if sentiment swings >0.33 in last 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% volatility buffer.
